elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14.3 retains "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA"; no New York choice of law was substituted.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered forum is "the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California" with exclusive submission; no New York County forum and no temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Retained original language: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions..." California is within the accepted fallback set; correctly left unchanged.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: AAA single-arbitrator San Francisco arbitration mechanic replaced with: "Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts." The forum corresponds to the retained California governing law, and the arbitration seat is fully removed (no residual award-entry or AAA-fee mechanic).

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: California law is retained untouched and the mandatory AAA arbitration forum is replaced by exclusive jurisdiction of the corresponding California state and federal courts, so the walk-away arbitration mechanic is eliminated.

Preferred level is not met (no New York law, no New York County exclusive forum, no temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out), which is acceptable because the redline is expressly targeted at the fallback and the finding is correctly classified as a deviation on the forum term only.

Minimality holds: only the jurisdiction/forum words changed. Deletion of the award-entry sentence and the AAA fee-allocation sentence is consequential rather than cosmetic, since both operate solely within the arbitration mechanic that the forum element requires be removed; retaining them would leave contradictory arbitration language. The heading edit from "Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue" to "Choice of Law; Venue" is conforming, and no extras (survival tails, fee-shifting, injunctive procedures, damages categories) were added.

Intent is preserved: the escrow-trigger dispute path in p0105 was conformed from "referred to arbitration in the manner provided in Section 14.3" to "referred to the courts designated in Section 14.3," so no dangling arbitration cross-reference or undefined term survives; the conflict-of-laws and CISG exclusions, the ten-business-day officer negotiation period, and the sixty-day cure mechanic are untouched.

Housekeeping note only (not a defect): the defined term "RULES" was introduced in the deleted arbitration sentence; the drafter should confirm no other section of the Agreement still references "Rules," otherwise that reference would be orphaned.
